title: Lazy Load

validation.research: Six authoritative source notes. Fowler’s Lazy Load catalog entry in Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture establishes partially loaded objects and four implementation variants: lazy initialization, virtual proxy, value holder, and ghost. Official SQLAlchemy documentation supports omitted columns, on-demand loading, N+1 query risks, eager strategies and unwanted-load guards, session lifetime, detached-instance failure, and thread/task ownership. Python documentation supports the demonstration’s explicit SQLite configuration. The article distinguishes deferred retrieval from successful-result retention, freshness, identity management, and authorization. The document scenario, manual reader, code, and native illustrations are original teaching material.
validation.python_examples: Both actual article fences execute as documents.py and demo.py and produce seven stated lines exactly. Checks cover omitted body payload in the initial SELECT, no body read before access, retained first success and callback release, empty text and NULL as loaded values, strict positive integer IDs, missing headers and invalid stored titles, failed body validation without publishing a value, repair and later success, missing rows at deferred access, propagated transient and storage failures without failure caching, independent wrappers and body caches, rejection after reader exit before SQL, loaded values after exit and connection closing, single-use lifecycle, caller-owned transaction and connection, and real cross-connection updates. The latter explicitly demonstrates an earlier header combined with a later body, and a retained body becoming stale. The counter measures body SELECTs, not all database queries. Sequential, non-reentrant access is required; no concurrency coordination or performance benchmark is claimed.

example_limits: Python 3.10+ and standard-library SQLite. Positive integer document IDs exclude booleans. Header titles must be text; body data may be text, empty text, or NULL. The reader selects only ID and title and captures the original ID in the body callback. A unique sentinel marks unloaded state. First success retains its value and releases the callback; failures propagate with the sentinel and callback intact, allowing another attempt while active but no automatic retry loop. The caller owns connection and transaction lifetime. Reader exit blocks new body reads before SQL, while loaded values remain usable. Unused wrappers retain callbacks and should not become long-lived reader handles. Separate wrappers have independent caches. There is no write API, identity map, refresh/invalidation, authorization, shared-thread/task coordination, recursive-loader protection, graph loader, or consistency/version protocol. Header and body observations need not be one snapshot, and retained data can become stale.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, push, or pull request.
